old_title: James has knee surgery; Martínez sorry; Watford sacking reports 'fake news': football - live
new_title: Carrick includes Martínez in squad; Madrid call for Tebas to quit over Goebbels comparison: football news - as it happened
old_text:
Thank you Simon, hello everyone. What a fantastic audience!
Football is happening around us, constantly, and this weekend is no different. There will be a wealth of Premier League manager press conferences coming up in the next few hours. And a ton of non-Premier League assocation football news and previews, too.
Right, I'm going to step away from the blog for a while. I leave you in the capable hands of Luke McLaughlin, who you can email here if you fancy. Back in a bit!
Dionisi says report of Watford sacking 'fake news'
Despite reports suggesting he would be sacked if Watford lost at Cardiff on Tuesday, Alessio Dionisi remains in post. "There is good news, bad news or fake news probably," the Italian told the BBC yesterday. "In this case for the moment, it is fake news. But I don't decide."
The situation at the club is dire: a squad haphazardly thrown together, with no money spent on transfer fees in the summer, the division's lowest wage bill, few players arriving until the final days of the window, a miserable dearth of Championship experience (which the club leadership acknowledged and pledged to address at the end of last season, and for that matter before most recent transfer windows), a disjointed and lopsided squad notably bereft of midfield options, and an aloof and increasingly unpopular owner.
Since the start of March the club have played 21 league games and won only three, the worst record of any club which has been in the division throughout that time (indeed Coventry, Ipswich, West Ham and Oxford United all have more wins and more Championship points despite spending much of it in other divisions). Most recently they played Burnley at home when their opponents were bottom of the league and lost 4-0, and then went to 21st-placed Cardiff and lost 5-1. They are now 22nd, and both Elton John - who said he was "upset and disappointed at the decline" - and Troy Deeney have criticised the way they are playing and the way they are being run.
Today Gino Pozzo is meeting a representative of fans' group the 1881 Movement - who recently published an open letter stating their "complete loss of confidence" in Pozzo, and criticising "the endless cycle of appointments and dismissals [which] has reduced a once-proud club to a source of ridicule". Tomorrow they host 13th-placed but also troubled Charlton, who won three of their first four league games but have not secured a victory since August.
Word is that the club has already made contact with potential replacements for Dionisi, but that the level of vitriol coming from those fans still sufficiently motivated to turn up to games has stayed Pozzo's hand, for now. The club certainly have some players, the likes of Othmane Maamma and Myron Boadu, who are able to play at a much higher level to the one the team is currently showing, but do they have the motivation (and the teammates) to demonstrate that ability, or has the cycle of sackings drained the squad of all motivation and cohesion?
Coventry boss Frank Lampard is not prepared to relax after watching his side record back-to-back wins in the Premier League, writes the Press Association.
The Sky Blues looked to be in for a long season after losing their opening four games without scoring a goal. But they have kick-started their campaign with wins against Nottingham Forest and Newcastle and as he prepares to visit Tottenham on Monday Lampard wants to keep the foot on the gas.
"Keep driving it," he said. "It's very important to look at the the good things out of the game, also the things we can improve. But when we talk about the good things, I'm not overly patting them on the back because we have to work hard to get better.
"Every game brings different challenges, so I think the players understand me and my approach and the staff's approach here. We never want to rest. I don't. I'm always fearful of resting on something and thinking that you've made it. This league's too difficult for that.
"So one of my first jobs is to keep pushing from that front, and the players need to feel that."
Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions.
Silva's substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices.
The worrying shift under Arbeloa was evident during Fulham's collapse against Ipswich last weekend. The west Londoners were 1-0 up and looking good for their first league win of the season when Arbeloa weakened his midfield by replacing Shea Charles with Manuel Ángel in the 70th minute.
It was a strange way to shut up shop. Charles is physically imposing, has impressed since joining from Southampton and was doing well alongside Sander Berge. The 22-year-old Ángel is 5ft 7in, was making his Premier League debut and has little experience of senior football. Ipswich's comeback to win 2-1 was not a surprise, particularly when Arbeloa's other rejigs included bringing on Rodrigo Muniz and switching from a 4-2-3-1 system to a flat 4-4-2 in an attempt to defend the lead.
Can you name the three teams still without a win in this season's Premier League? If so, you're approximately 6.7% of the way to full marks in the sports quiz of the week!
Fulham's Alvaro Arbeloa has held his press conference ahead of tomorrow's home game against Hull, and has been quizzed on how confident he is that he will still be at the club in a week's time if they are not able to win:
I am focused on tomorrow's game, on my players, on my team, that is the most important thing. It's not about me, it's about the club, it's about the players, it's about the supporters. For me it's been a normal week. We've been working hard. We were preparing for a difficult match against a very difficult team.
I saw the commitment of the players this week, how they have been training. They are so focused on tomorrow's game. I saw them, how they can play. For me it is the most important thing, the performance of the players. It's not about my future, it's about the club and about the players. They are looking for their reward, and looking for a game where they can get a win for our supporters and I think they deserve it.
Donald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leader awarded the Fifa peace prize after Gianni Infantino was told at Thursday's meeting of Fifa council to make major changes or scrap the controversial award.
The Guardian has learned that several council members demanded the award be abolished and others called for the prize to be depoliticised, with Fifa's football social responsibility committee to make a recommendation before the next council meeting in Doha on 16 December.
The Women's Super League table is taking shape for 2026-27. The defending champions, Manchester City, have five wins from five games but more intriguing stories lie elsewhere. Why are Arsenal struggling, who is performing better than results suggest, and in which way are two promoted teams smashing expectations? Andrew Beasley has the answers:
Chelsea have announced that Reece James has had "successful" and "minor" surgery on a knee injury sustained in training. "Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club's medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase," the club wrote on social media.
Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle says he is uninterested in dwelling on what might have been when highly-rated Aston Villa midfielder Johan Manzambi visits St James' Park this weekend, writes the Press Association.
Manzambi looked set for a switch to Tyneside over the summer but the deal was hijacked as Villa swooped in to sign the Switzerland international, who has flourished during his short time in the midlands.
The 21-year-old opened the scoring in Villa's 6-0 Champions League rout of Fenerbahce in midweek and he could rub salt into his former suitors' wounds when Newcastle welcome Unai Emery's side on Saturday.
But while Jaissle, who succeeded Eddie Howe after Manzambi snubbed a move to the north-east, is a fan of the youngster, the German side-stepped the question of whether he would have liked him in his ranks.
"He is a really good player," said Jaissle, who will be looking for a response after Monday's 4-1 loss at Coventry. "But I'm not here to talk now about players, about rumours, about potential signings. The pure focus is on our players. We have many things to do, many things to improve, and that's the approach to not get distracted by anything else."
Joelinton is poised for his first start of the season for Newcastle on Saturday while Dan Burn looks set to be on the bench again, with Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey poised to return to light training next week.
Is there a correlation between running more and winning more in the Premier League, I wonder? We have the answer for you! And it is, to summarise, um, kind of but not really but maybe a bit. Read about it, with graphs and everything, here:
Hello world, and happy Friday! Yes, we are all one day closer to finding out if there are any new depths for our teams still to plumb, which is certainly an exciting prospect for my fellow Watford fans. In unusual coincidence news, this Premier League weekend sees all four English teams who were in action in Europe last night play each other on Sunday - Bournemouth v Sunderland, Brighton v Crystal Palace - while the two Scottish teams who played in Europe last night also play each other on Sunday, with Hearts heading to Celtic. Meanwhile table-topping, relegation-bound Manchester City host Ipswich and second-placed Arsenal head to Nottingham Forest, while Fulham and Spurs, like Bournemouth winless in the league this season, seek those magic three points at home to promoted teams, Fulham v Hull on Saturday and Spurs v Coventry on Monday.
But we get the ball rolling with an apology, after Lisandro Martínez begged forgiveness not for what he said about the shambles at Manchester United, but for the fact that the "time and place ... perhaps were not the right ones", which the way I read it is very much a partial climbdown rather than the fulsome version that some are interpreting it as. Anyway, read all about it!

I will leave you with details of all our coverage of another bumper weekend of sporting action, coming up tomorrow and on Sunday. May your team score a last-minute winner, or at least bring you joy of some sort. Goodbye.
Real Madrid call for Tebas to resign over Goebbels comparison
Real Madrid have again demanded the resignation of the president of La Liga after he compared the club's efforts to discredit referees with the propaganda techniques of the Nazi Germany.
Javier Tebas lashed out at Madrid on Friday on social media with a long post that criticised how its club television channel says referees hurt its chances of winning. The channel regularly runs reels of what it considers gross errors by match officials who are set to work upcoming games for the 15-time European champions.
Tebas compared the tactic with those used by Joseph Goebbels, the minister of propaganda in Nazi Germany during the second world war.
"The Sporting Events Bill delivers on the government's 2024 manifesto commitment to deliver international events with pride, to seek new opportunities where we can, creating a legacy to inspire the next generation of talent while promoting exercise and healthy living.
"At its core, the bill will establish a UK-wide, event-agnostic framework to enable the UK government and devolved governments to meet common binding guarantees required by rights holders for major sporting events, such as the UEFA EURO 2028 Football Championships and the 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup, should our bid be successful."
The Liberal Democrats have tabled an amendment to the Sporting Events Bill, currently at the committee stage, that would compel the Premier League to expel Manchester City, if the club's guilty verdict over financial misdemeanours is confirmed on appeal.
"Financial integrity of participating teams and penalties for disguised funding (1) A sporting team or organisation participating in a qualifying sporting event designated under section 2 must maintain financial integrity and compliance with applicable financial regulations. (2) A person or body corporate commits an offence if, in connection with their participation in or qualification for a qualifying sporting event, they- (a) submit false, inaccurate or misleading financial accounts or commercial contracts to a governing body or national authority; or (b) operate a scheme to disguise equity funding, owner contributions, or third-party payments as commercial sponsorship or revenue. (3) Where an enforcement authority is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that a person or body corporate has contravened subsection (1) or(2), the enforcement authority must disqualify the sporting team from competing in the designated event. (4) In this section, "disguised funding" means any payment, contribution, or financial benefit provided directly or indirectly by a connected party, owner, or state entity that is mischaracterised in official accounts as arms-length commercial revenue; "qualifying sporting event" means a major sporting event to which the framework under section 2 has been applied."
"No. I don't comment on what happens in other clubs," says Farke. "For that, no comment, to this topic. I just rate it a bit in a different way, when the perception is a bit negative, there is always chance for a hurt boxer to change the momentum again.
"They have the qualities to be very competitive in this game. I expect a very difficult home game for us. No comments about anything in their camp. We have to concentrate on bringing our strengths to the pitch ... if we do so, we have a chance to win some points.
"You need to use the emotions in the stadium, perhaps for this extra per cent, the extra yard ... Playing with fire in the heart but also cool in the head is also important. If you burn too early, even a few days before the game, like a candle from both sides, you won't burn enough during the game."
"I am not sure we are favourites [against Manchester United] ... we've had a brilliant start to this season ... perhaps many [other clubs] have found it tough ... but if you have a look at the squads ... you have to say they are definitely not the underdog in a game against Leeds United ... it's still a very dangerous opponent, even more dangerous when they come off the back of a few games without a win ... we have to be at the top of our game."
"Joe [Rodon] will miss this game," says Farke. "We said this injury would last eight to 10 weeks. I think we are right now in week seven. So he's edging closer, he's making good progress with his rehab work [but] not in contention for this game.
"Daniel James ... since yesterday he's back on the pitch with us. Right now we have to wait how his body reacts ... but good news, he is back in training and seems to be improved ... we have to wait and see how he comes through the last two sessions but there is a chance he is involved."
Let's enjoy a dash of Daniel Farke, whose Leeds team face crisis club Manchester United at Elland Road on Sunday. Allow me a moment to type up some quotes from here.
Speaking earlier, the Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage said his players need to manage the emotions of the "derby" against Brighton on the south coast on Sunday, telling them to play smart.
"This team [Brighton] has strengths ... and weaknesses too," Sage said. "We have to be really smart in our way of playing for this game. We have to be not only in a "rivalry" game, but in a smart game."
Michael Carrick brushed off Lisandro Martínez not offering Jason Wilcox a public apology after the defender criticised Manchester United's director of football in the wake of Tuesday's defeat at Atlético Madrid.
Martínez referred directly to Wilcox after the 2-0 Champions League loss, saying: "I expect more from our technical director.
On Thursday Martínez issued an apology that did not mention Wilcox or withdraw the essence of his outburst: the need for more squad investment. "The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise," he said.
Carrick was asked whether he respected Martínez for not saying sorry to Wilcox. "He's released his statement, he's realised he's made a mistake and that's enough for all of us to move on with," United's manager said.
Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal's decision to cut up to 60 jobs and insisted it was necessary to ensure they can continue achieving success.
The Premier League champions are understood to have informed some, but not all, of the staff whose positions are at risk after a consultation process started by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) before the end of last season. Arsenal hope the number of redundancies can be reduced and will attempt to redeploy affected employees wherever possible, although some job losses may be unavoidable.
Real Madrid demand 'immediate resignation' of La Liga president over Goebbels comparisons
Real Madrid has again demanded the resignation of Javier Tebas, the president of La Liga, after he compared the club's efforts to discredit referees with the propaganda techniques of the German Nazi regime, writes AP.
Javier Tebas lashed out at Madrid on Friday on social media with a long post that criticized its club television channel's habit of running reels of what it considers glaring errors by match officials who are set to work their upcoming games. Tebas compared the tactic with those of Joseph Goebbels, the minister of propaganda in World War II Nazi Germany.
"The executive of Real Madrid has an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid leads the way," Tebas wrote. "Its script is always the same: select plays that favour it, repeat the alleged affront, increase suspicion and name enemies. It reminds one of the propaganda techniques that Goebbels used."
Tebas added "the comparison is with the techniques, not with the ideology or, of course, with Madrid fans."
Madrid responded by saying in a statement that Tebas, who has clashed several times over the years with club president Florentino Pérez, was unfit to hold his job representing Spain's top clubs, demanding his "immediate resignation."
"Javier Tebas's repeated conduct demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect, and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities," it said. "His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those demanding transparency and regeneration represent, in our club's view, a genuine scourge for Spanish football."
Coach Jose Mourinho has also voiced complaints that Madrid, which holds a record 36 Spanish league titles, is regularly hurt by referees.
In September, Madrid demanded Tebas step down after he criticized the club for attacking the refereeing crew in the 2-1 loss at Atletico Madrid .
In Friday's statement, Madrid repeated its complaint that Tebas hasn't done enough over the ongoing judicial probe into Barcelona's alleged payments to an official on the refereeing committee of the Spanish soccer federation for several years.
Ipswich's Gary O'Neill has revealed what he thinks of the situation regarding Manchester City's Premier League future, and their appeal against guilty verdicts for breaching the league's financial regulations. And it is, to summarise, nothing much:
I suppose any off-field situation, not just this one, that rumbles on or takes a while, everyone involves in the competition wants sorted, because we want everything to be decided on the pitch. You just want clarity. But as far as I'm concerned, it's so far away from a priority for me to even know or care what is happening at Manchester City.
"Throughout the proceedings, the RFEF has maintained that it acted immediately, diligently and effectively from the moment it became aware of the incidents," a high-ranking official in the RFEF told Reuters.
"Furthermore, the measures taken ensured that the chants were not repeated and that the spectators present in the stadium themselves expressed their disapproval of such behaviour."
The official said the federation considered the sanctions particularly severe, arguing that comparable capacity restrictions had not been imposed automatically in more serious cases or those involving previous disciplinary offences.
Reuters has contacted FIFA for comment.
The chants were detected by the RFEF's monitoring systems and immediately reported to the match officials, the official said, adding that security was reinforced in the affected section of the stadium.
"The Federation cooperated fully with the relevant authorities to identify those responsible."
Oliver Glasner has spoken ahead of Nottingham Forest's game against Arsenal on Sunday, and has revealed exactly what he thinks about the Gunners. To summarise: they are good.
Huge credit to Mikel Arteta and to Arsenal. It's now a team that has been built over years, at the beginning finding a core and then always adding the right pieces. It's not only the quality it's the mentality. In every game this season they're outrunning the opposition. The effort, the mindset Mikel created there is incredible and this makes it so tough to play against them. And of course they have so many world-class players they can react from the bench.
This is what we are facing. The structure, how they are playing, everybody knows and analyses but the way they are executing it makes it so difficult. It's a huge challenge. But on the other side that's exactly what we need to improve our game, and to show that we are ready.
Mikel Arteta has explained why Arsenal took their official team photo this week without William Saliba, who had a doctor's appointment when the photographer turned up:
What happened was that we tried to do that picture three times already and we had to cancel it last minute for different reasons, and we had some commercial obligations so we decided to do it. We will retake the picture with the whole family. Willy, normally he's happy about everything and he knows how loved he is and he is completely fine.
Spain have been fined and told to partially close the stadium hosting their next international friendly after Islamophobic chanting was heard during a match against Egypt earlier this year, writes the Press Association.
A section of Spain fans chanted "whoever doesn't jump is a Muslim" during the friendly in Barcelona on March 31, with anti-discrimination messages displayed on the big screens and announcements made at half-time urging fans to stop the chants.
The Spanish federation (RFEF) sought to have the disciplinary process thrown out, in part on the grounds that the word Muslim is the accepted term for a follower of Islam.
However, Fifa's disciplinary committee concluded the chants "clearly use religious identity as a means of distinguishing and discriminating against the opposing side" and said a reasonable and objective observer would see the word "Muslim" used in this context "as a marker of exclusion and ridicule".
The RFEF has been fined $20,000 (£15,000) and ordered to close 15% of the stadium for their next men's senior team friendly, or fill that percentage of seats with community or special interest groups, such as families, students and anti-discrimination organisations, subject to Fifa's approval.
Spain star Lamine Yamal said at the time he found the chants "intolerable" as a Muslim himself, adding: "I understand not all fans are like this, but to those who sing these things, using a religion as a mockery on the field makes you ignorant and racist people. Football is to be enjoyed and encouraged, not to disrespect people for who they are or what they believe in."
Pierre Sage is asked for an update on Crystal Palace's injured or potentially injured players. "I don't know because we will train after the press conference," he says. "For the moment we hope, but we don't know." Well that's cleared that up then.
David Moyes has had a chat with the media ahead of tomorrow's lunchtimely game against Chelsea. "I'm not an expert on Chelsea," he says. Oh. He's then asked about his personal future, and the chance of him signing a new contract to replace his current one, which expires at the end of this season:
I'm getting on with the job and trying to build Everton and keep it going in the right direction. Hopefully we've done some half decent things in the last year and a half or so. So, we'll see. There's been plenty of talks happening through the summer. Maybe at the moment there's just a little bit of a lull. But as I've said many times, it's not the most important thing for me.
Emery says he is having a whole lot of fun this season:
More than last year even. Because when we were building the team in a successful year, it was fantastic. But then we were not changing so much the squad, and we had a lot of challenges and I was enjoying how we were achieving, the good performances. But this year especially more because we changed it more than normal. And we have a lot of players, how they can connect, with their style of play, to be strong and to be closer to winning. How we have won against Fenerbahce was fantastic. But we have a lot of work to do and improve.
Unai Emery demonstrates his grasp of English idiom when asked about Aston Villa's development:
John Toshack said, 'Don't avoid the trees not permitting you to see the forest.' This phrase is fantastic to use in this situation. We have a lot of things to improve. A lot of things to add, to build our structure as strong as possible. I think I explained well.
Keith Andrews: 'We've just got really good players'
Keith Andrews is asked why Mamadou Sangaré isn't starting for Brentford. "I haven't spoken much about that with the coach," Sangaré said this week. "He's the coach, he's the boss. I'm a player like so many others. It's not only about me here. The most important thing is the team. That's what counts." And here's what Andrews says:
We've got a really good squad, really good options. It's difficult picking a team. My main message to the squad is, it's going to be a long season. We're going to need everybody. We've just got really good players.
Hello again! I bring a bit more news from Enzo Maresca, who has had to spend a surprising amount of his press conference dealing with banana-based queries. He is, in short, supportive. "I didn't know the history behind the bananas. I hope tomorrow I can see many bananas in the stadium," he trilled. "I think it creates a nice environment for everyone in the stadium."
"I hope so," says Alonso. "Our goal is to keep doing that [scoring at this rate]. If we improve the level of scoring, and decrease numbers of conceding, we will be in a better way ... tomorrow at Everton will be tough ... I haven't been to this stadium but they tell me it's a nice one, with good atmosphere. I am looking forward to it.
"I want that we compete. We know it's tough to win games away ... but we are able to deal with that ... for sure, the experience against Brentford is not forgotten."
Potentially unpopular personal opinion alert: Perhaps Chelsea are outscoring their xG because xG is meaningless nonsense?
Will Chelsea's activity in the January transfer window be affected by James's injury?
"No. I don't think so," says Alonso. "We expect for that time he is back ... the timeline is not exact. But it will not affect it [activity in the January window.]
"He's the captain. A very important player. He has a good mentality. We need him."
James absence 'not going to be short', says Chelsea's Alonso
"We are disappointed, especially for him," the Chelsea manager says of Reece James's surgery on a knee injury. "In the last training he picked up an injury ... but now the surgery has been successful ... he will be close to the team, he is a great influence. We wish him the best recovery. We don't set timelines, but he will be out for several weeks.
"It's not going to be short. It's not going to be two-three weeks ... time will tell. Things have to be done properly ... it's a disappointment for everyone, for him ... we have a squad for that, to deal with the injuries.
"We have until the next break, four more Premier League games, a Cup game ... we will be able to manage well with the players we have ... we feel good."
Has Maresca sought guidance on the current situation from anyone outside Manchester City?
"I am quite a 'respect' person," Maresca says. "Everyone can say what they want ... I don't have a problem with people having an opinion ... [but] I think it's better to wait for the final words [the result of City's appeal].
"I trust the club. I don't need people from outside the club to understand the situation ... they explained the situation. It's very clear. I trust them [City's owners], this is the reason I joined the club.
"There is a lot of outside noise. We need to try and make our own noise. The different kind of noise, we are not able to control that."
Pep Guardiola was at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday for the Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain. Did Maresca speak to him?
"I saw him after the game. We were talking about the game, about the first half, about the second half ... he was very happy to be at the stadium, very positive about things he has seen during the game ... it was great for the fans to see him at the stadium ... this will always be his house.
Maresca feels 'no stress' about off-field issues at City
"Very happy. very pleased. Two big games, Liverpool away and PSG at home [in the past week]. We handled quite good, I think all together - the club, fans, teams, everyone. Tomorrow it's the same points [on offer against Ipswich] as Anfield. That's why it's important we try to win.
"I am very happy. I don't feel any kind of stress about the outside situation [verdict on financial charges]. It's something I don't control. I focus on how we can try to win the next games.
On Phil Foden: "He will score tomorrow. I just try to work with him, day by day. Since the international break, since the red card, he's training well. Very positive, very good. He is available for tomorrow. No doubt he is going to give us something."

Spain have been fined and told to partially close the stadium hosting their next international friendly after Islamophobic chanting was heard during a match against Egypt earlier this year, writes the Press Association. A section of Spain fans chanted "whoever doesn't jump is a Muslim" during the friendly in Barcelona on March 31, with anti-discrimination messages displayed on the big screens and announcements made at half-time urging fans to stop the chants. The Spanish federation (RFEF) sought to have the disciplinary process thrown out, in part on the grounds that the word Muslim is the accepted term for a follower of Islam. However, Fifa's disciplinary committee concluded the chants "clearly use religious identity as a means of distinguishing and discriminating against the opposing side" and said a reasonable and objective observer would see the word "Muslim" used in this context "as a marker of exclusion and ridicule". The RFEF has been fined $20,000 (£15,000) and ordered to close 15% of the stadium for their next men's senior team friendly, or fill that percentage of seats with community or special interest groups, such as families, students and anti-discrimination organisations, subject to Fifa's approval. Spain star Lamine Yamal said at the time he found the chants "intolerable" as a Muslim himself, adding: "I understand not all fans are like this, but to those who sing these things, using a religion as a mockery on the field makes you ignorant and racist people. Football is to be enjoyed and encouraged, not to disrespect people for who they are or what they believe in."
